start.text: A cart comes out of the brambles. The canes lift for it and settle behind, and an old man in a sacking smock pulls it down the cart road in plain daylight, sacks roped on the bed, a rake across the top.
Hob Marl stops at the edge of the camp and looks at the sky as if he'd forgotten it had a colour.
Road's a road. Road's a road. I said I'd come in.
Bram Kettle is already coming across the yard, wiping his hands. He stops short.
Hob. Hob Marl. Kettle's on. You'll hate it.
Morning, old-timer. Can I help you?
Salt. Bram Kettle. Big lad. Mother was Saltmarrow. You know me. You... You don't know me.
Bram looks at the old man a long moment, then at you, as if you might explain it. You can't. Not to him.
There's salt in the store. Take a crock. Take two. I don't know why. Take them.
Hob leaves the cart by the sacks on the jetty and sits on the tally-house step with his rake across his knees. He doesn't look back at the ridge.

Hob leaves the cart by the sacks on the jetty and sits on the tally-house step with his rake across his knees. Now and then he looks back up at the ridge, at the light, and counts something on his fingers.
